paper.title: Algorithm 745: Computation of the complete and incomplete Fermi-Dirac integral

stack: Fortran 77 (TOMS 745 archive 745.gz: FERTST.IN, FERTST.OUT and src.f, with the authors' own test main program FERTST in src.f)

claim.text: The authors' FERTST driver computes FERMID(ORD=0.5, X=5.0) for the row registered in FERTST.IN (FERMID block, row 17); the value must equal the shipped reference 8.8442088952430 to relative tolerance 1e-10 (fixed in the queue entry; recorded here as the absolute tolerance 8.8442088952430e-10 at that value).

reference.archive: netlib.org/toms/745.gz sha256 575d82e32dfdbe780834f0d7cfb49bfd82f8394fd25c50c9c40cc7daccf89ae0 (member FERTST.IN, FERMID block, row ORD=0.5D+00 X=5.0D+00)

attempt: Reproduced at the registered claim, under a build flag. As shipped, src.f built with gfortran (-O0 and -O2) runs to the end but gives FERMID(0.5, 5.0) = 3.1115013689941 (not 8.8442088952430), and 15 of the 36 FERMID rows disagree with their shipped references (several are NaN); the same 15 rows at both optimisation levels. The shipped FERTST.OUT, the authors' own run, matches the reference. A diagnostic build with -finit-local-zero (evidence/diagnostic-uninit.txt) gives 8.8442088952430 for the claimed point and all 36 FERMID rows within 1e-10 relative, so the difference is consistent with a local variable that src.f reads before it is set (undefined behaviour) which the authors' compiler happened to leave zero. Which variable is not isolated (gfortran -Wall reports none; FDPOS reads LOGGAM only after it is set on one path). The verdict uses the build flag -finit-local-zero, which changes no source byte (build-only: manifests pre, mid and post are equal over the sources). It is therefore a patched result (grade B), not an original run; the as-shipped mismatch is the original attempt. Both optimisation levels with the flag give the same value (pass 1 -O0, pass 2 -O2).

original_attempt.reason: src.f compiled as shipped (gfortran -O0 and -O2) and run on the shipped FERTST.IN: it runs to the end, but FERMID(0.5, 5.0) = 3.1115013689941 against the reference 8.8442088952430, and 15 of 36 FERMID rows disagree. So the authors' code, run as documented under this toolchain, does not give the claimed value; the claim was reproduced only with the build flag.
